How we choose

Every place is recommended by named sources (review-aggregator star ratings never count as the recommender), pinned to its door from a published coordinate, and status-checked. Closed places stay, flagged, so you know they’re gone.

Must see
The places to plan a visit around — graded within each area, not across the city.
Worth the detour
Strong picks, worth going out of your way for.
Deep cut
For the curious: smaller, odder, more local.

Within each area, places are ordered by tier, then by number of named sources — never by popularity. Numbers on the cards match the pins on the map. No ratings, prices or opening hours are shown, because the guide doesn’t hold verified ones.

124 sights and 201 places to eat from Fort Lauderdale down through Miami-Dade to Everglades and Biscayne national parks, each traceable to the source that named it. The food runs on what South Florida does best: the Cuban sandwich and a ventanita cafecito, croquetas and pastelitos, stone crab, Haitian griot, Peruvian ceviche, arepas, key lime pie, Redland tropical fruit, and gator and frog legs at the edge of the Glades.

How this guide was made

How the cuisine filters were policed

Every food card names a specific dish — a cuisine label alone doesn’t qualify. The region’s canon comes first: the Cuban sandwich and medianoche, croquetas, pastelitos and the ventanita cafecito, the frita, stone crab, Haitian griot, Peruvian ceviche, arepas, key lime pie, conch, Nicaraguan fritanga, Redland tropical fruit, and gator and frog legs at the Glades edge. A cuisine tag names the kitchen’s own tradition, never one dish it happens to serve.

Web-searched, merit-measured and fact-checked

Every place is traceable to at least two credible sources (or one institutional authority — Michelin, James Beard, the National Park Service) — the Miami Herald, Miami New Times, the Sun Sentinel, Eater Miami, The Infatuation, WLRN, Time Out, the Greater Miami and Fort Lauderdale tourism boards, Florida State Parks, Atlas Obscura and vetted creators — recorded in data/sources.json. Yelp, TripAdvisor and Google ratings never count as a recommender. Every coordinate is verified into data/geocodes.json and every place status-checked.
